hate_speech_law.t: Government shouldn't punish speech, however hateful, unless it threatens or incites violence, as today.
yes: Protecting hateful speech under the First Amendment
no: Fines or jail for hateful speech

hate_speech_law.t: Only the most extreme public hateful speech should be a crime, such as calling a group subhuman.
yes: Narrow hate speech laws for the most extreme speech

hate_speech_law.t: Hateful public speech about race, religion, sexual orientation or gender identity should bring fines or jail.
yes: Hate speech laws like those in much of Europe

hateful_speaker_response.t: Answer hateful speech with more speech; don't try to silence the speaker.
Criticism and boycotts are fair, but the speaker shouldn't lose their job or platform.
Platforms, venues and employers should drop the speaker.
The law should punish hateful speech.
no: Leaving it to public response alone

campus_speakers: A public university should allow this talk: {case}.
A public university shouldn't allow this talk: {case}.

flag_burning.t: Burning the flag in protest should stay legal as protected speech.
yes: The 1989 Supreme Court ruling as it stands

flag_burning.t: Flag burning should be legal, but cities can ban open fires in some places for safety.
yes: Fire-safety rules that apply to all fires
no: Bans aimed at flag burning itself

flag_burning.t: Amend the Constitution to allow a flag-burning ban.
yes: A constitutional amendment banning flag burning
no: Treating flag burning as protected speech

protest_masks.t: Masks at protests should be legal; anonymity protects protesters from retaliation.
Masks at protests should be illegal only while committing a crime.
Wearing a mask to hide your identity at any protest should be illegal.

campus_encampments.t: Public universities should allow protest camps as long as they stay peaceful.
Allow protest camps only for a limited time in designated areas.
yes: Time and place limits on camps

gov_misinformation.t: Government shouldn't judge what's true online.
yes: No government role on false claims
no: Government corrections, flags or removal demands

gov_misinformation.t: Government should only publish its own corrections.
yes: Official corrections on health and election claims

gov_misinformation.t: Government should flag false posts, but not require removal.
yes: Government flags on false health and election posts

gov_misinformation.t: Government should require platforms to remove posts its agencies find false on topics like health and elections.
yes: Required removal of posts agencies judge false

misinfo_penalty.t: No new penalties for spreading false information beyond fraud and defamation law.
no: New fines or jail for false claims

misinfo_penalty.t: Penalties only for knowingly false claims about when, where or how to vote.
Fines or jail for knowingly spreading harmful false claims.
yes: Penalties for false claims about medicines, disasters and similar topics

jawboning.t: Officials should never pressure social media companies over legal speech.
yes: Barring officials from takedown requests over legal posts

jawboning.t: Officials can ask for takedowns only for clear legal violations, like threats.
Officials can ask for takedowns, but every request must be public.
yes: Public logs of every government takedown request

jawboning.t: Officials can ask for takedowns, and companies decide.
yes: Officials flagging posts they consider harmful

library_book_decisions.t: School librarians should decide on challenged books, using professional standards.
A committee of librarians, teachers and parents should decide.
The elected school board should decide.
yes: School board votes on challenged books

library_book_decisions.t: A challenged book should come off the shelves during review; one objection is enough.
yes: Pulling books on a single objection pending review

library_explicit.t: High school libraries should carry literary novels with explicit sex, freely available.
Students should need parent permission to check out novels with explicit sex.
High school libraries shouldn't carry novels with explicit sex.

employer_speech.t: The law should protect workers from being fired for political views expressed outside work.
no: Firing over personal posts or views

employer_speech.t: Employers can fire over outside political speech only if it directly harms the business.
yes: Firing only when the business is harmed

employer_speech.t: Employers should be free to fire workers for political views.

employer_speech_cases: An employer shouldn't be able to fire someone for this: {case}.
An employer should be able to fire someone for this: {case}.

defamation_public_figures.t: Keep today's high bar for public figures suing news outlets.
Make it somewhat easier for public figures to sue news outlets.
Make it much easier: proving a story was false and harmful should be enough.

public_broadcasting.t: Fund public radio and TV more than in the past.
yes: Increased federal funding for public broadcasting

public_broadcasting.t: Fund public radio and TV about as in the past.
No federal funding for public broadcasting.
yes: Ending federal money for public radio and TV

campus_speech_codes.t: Public universities should be able to discipline students for offensive speech.
Discipline only for repeated offensive speech aimed at a specific person.
Public universities shouldn't discipline students for offensive speech.
